sections.overview: The common redshank is a widespread Eurasian wader that breeds in wet open country and winters on coasts and estuaries.
sections.identification: Its bright orange-red legs stand out.
sections.habitat: It breeds in wet meadows and marshes, and winters mainly on coasts and estuaries.
sections.diet: It takes insects, worms and spiders when breeding, and also eats molluscs, crustaceans and occasionally small fish or tadpoles.
sections.behavior: It probes or pecks for prey and often feeds in flocks on open shores, especially around high tide.
sections.reproduction: It usually lays four eggs in a shallow ground nest; the chicks can walk and feed soon after leaving it.
sections.ecology: The spotted redshank can resemble it in winter, but its longer bill and lack of a white wing-bar separate the two.
sections.conservation: Oiseaux.net lists it as globally Least Concern, while the BTO reports declining and increasingly fragmented British breeding populations.
